annotations.derivable_answer: In Keshet and Abney's description-based account, a pronoun carries the presupposition that its corresponding antecedent description is instantiated in each world of the context set. It is implemented via Plural Intensional Presuppositional predicate calculus (PIP).

supporting_quotations.quote:
We propose that a pronoun presupposes that its corresponding
antecedent description is instantiated in each world of the context set. For instance,
there must be a cheeseburger being eaten by Andrea in every candidate world of
the context set in order for It is large to be felicitous after Andrea might be eating
a cheeseburger. We implement our proposal via a new logic (building on work
by Keshet (2018) and Abney & Keshet (2022)) that we name Plural Intensional
Presuppositional predicate calculus (or PIP).

annotations.rationale: Passage 1 explicitly details both the pronoun presupposition and the PIP formal logic.

annotations.derivable_answer: Gemini 3.1 Pro costs up to 1,431x as much as a comparable embedding model. LLMs maintain a distinct lead on reasoning-heavy (or reasoning-intensive) retrieval.

supporting_quotations.quote:
Gemini 3.1 Pro costs 1,431 × as much as a comparable
embedding model, and the gap persists across hardware scenarios. Reasoning
contributes substantially to this asymmetry. Lower reasoning budgets preserve or
improve retrieval for most evaluated models (§4.4–4.6). 4. Throughput lags by orders of magnitude, even on the same hardware.Served
on an identical H100, open-weight LLMs process 2.5–736× fewer tokens per second than embedding models, consistent with the architectural difference between
autoregressive generation and a single encoder pass (§4.5; Figure 7). LLMs and embedding models therefore serve complementary roles. Embedding pipelines
remain the efficient default for classification, similarity, and clustering; LLMs are most
useful for reasoning-intensive retrieval.

annotations.rationale: Passage 1 specifies both the cost ratio (1,431x as much as a comparable embedding model) and the task category where LLMs maintain their lead (reasoning-intensive retrieval).

annotations.derivable_answer: GeoCache borrows the core principle of reverse reprojection caching (reusing previously computed shading values by warping them to the current viewpoint via reprojection and validating temporal consistency) to reuse diffusion features across adjacent viewpoints in 3D generation trajectories.

supporting_quotations.quote:
Reverse reprojection
caching (Nehab et al. 2007) provides a closer computational
pattern by transporting a per-pixel quantity through geometric correspondence, integrating it into the target pixel’s retained value, and periodically refreshing the result. GeoCache applies these operations inside a denoising trajectory
and transports a first difference inx0 across views of the
same object.

annotations.rationale: Passage 1 explicitly explains how GeoCache borrows from reverse reprojection caching to reuse computations across multi-view diffusion trajectories.

annotations.derivable_answer: Attachment styles are measured using the 36-item ECR-R scale (18 items assessing attachment anxiety and 18 assessing attachment avoidance). ECBench was developed because while ECR-R captures attachment tendencies via self-report assessment, it may not fully reflect performance in realistic relational interactions across multi-turn conversations.

supporting_quotations.quote:
Following the original scoring procedure, selected items are reverse scored so that higher scores consistently indicate
stronger anxious or avoidant tendencies. For model evaluation, we present the ECR-R
items to each model individually and require responses within a ﬁxed set of options. We then
compute the mean scores for anxiety and avoidance and map them onto a two-dimensional attachment space. Speciﬁcally, we use the midpoint of 4
on the seven-point scale as the threshold: scores at
or below 4 are treated as low and scores above 4
as high. Based on the resulting combination, each
model is classiﬁed as secure, preoccupied, dismissing, or fearful ( Fraley et al. , 2000).

The ECR-R characterize the attachment tendencies of LLMs, but lacks realistic interpersonal interaction contexts. We therefore introduce a dialogue benchmark called ECBench for evaluating
emotional companionship capabilities in realistic
interaction scenarios.

annotations.rationale: Passage 1 specifies the 36-item ECR-R scale and Passage 2 explains why ECBench was developed to evaluate realistic relational interactions.
